description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:
1. Use search_investigators with condition and location to find PIs
2. Extract investigator names from results

Use this server to access comprehensive data on clinical trials including study design,
eligibility criteria, enrollment information, outcome measures, locations, and results.

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:
• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"

## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## plugin:browser-use:browser-use
# This MCP server

These rules override the skill below where they differ:
- Code runs in browser_exec; there is no shell, so ignore `BU_NAME=... browser-use <<'PY'` examples.
- Local: without a cloud browser, browser_exec drives the user's own Chrome; where none can be attached (no Chrome installed, Linux with no display, or remote debugging off in Chrome) its own Chromium on a temp profile instead. The first browser_exec result says which, and how to get the user's Chrome.
- Cloud: `start_remote_daemon()` (call browser_login first if not signed in). Every later browser_exec and

  uses: a name passed to start_remote_daemon / stop_remote_daemon is ignored.
- It lives 30 minutes unless you pass `timeout=<minutes>` (up to 240), and this server stops it when it
  exits. Once it ends, calls fail with an error: start a new one, never fall back to the local Chrome.
- Code runs in this server's process: it can read the server's environment (BROWSER_USE_API_KEY when set) and files.
- The live view and CDP URLs grant control of the browser, so they are not shown. Only if the user asks to watch, run

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timed-out `scroll(...)` on an attached background tab is evide… [truncated]
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

def parse_function_tool_arguments(
    *,
    input_tools: Iterable[ToolParam] | Omit | None,
    function_call: ParsedResponseFunctionToolCall | ResponseFunctionToolCall,
) -> object:
    if input_tools is None or not is_given(input_tools):
        return None

    input_tool = get_input_tool_by_name(
        input_tools=input_tools, name=function_call.name, namespace=function_call.namespace
    )
    if not input_tool:
        return None

    tool = cast(object, input_tool)
    if isinstance(tool, ResponsesPydanticFunctionTool):
        return model_parse_json(tool.model, function_call.arguments)

    if not input_tool.get("strict"):
        return None

    return json.loads(function_call.arguments)

5408 def _convert_responses_chunk_to_generation_chunk(
5409 chunk: Any,
5410 current_index: int, # index in content
5411 current_output_index: int, # index in Response output
5412 current_sub_index: int, # index of content block in output item
5413 schema: type[_BM] | None = None,
5414 metadata: dict | None = None,
5415 has_reasoning: bool = False,
5416 output_version: str | None = None,
5417 item_output_indices: dict[str, int] | None = None, # item id -> `output_index`
5418 ) -> tuple[int, int, int, ChatGenerationChunk | None]:
5419 # After several built-in tool calls the API can report a later `output_index` on
5420 # an item's `done` events than on its `added` event. Pin each item to the first
5421 # `output_index` seen so its events keep landing on the same content block.
5422 item_id = getattr(getattr(chunk, "item", None), "id", None) or getattr(
5423 chunk, "item_id", None
5424 )
5425 if (
5426 item_output_indices is not None
5427 and item_id is not None
5428 and (stream_output_index := getattr(chunk, "output_index", None)) is not None
5429 ):
5430 item_output_indices.setdefault(item_id, stream_output_index)
5431
5432 def _advance(output_idx: int, sub_idx: int | None = None) -> None:
5433 """Advance indexes tracked during streaming.
5434
5435 Example: we stream a response item of the form:
5436
5437 ```python
5438 {
5439 "type": "message", # output_index 0
5440 "role": "assistant",
5441 "id": "msg_123",
5442 "content": [
5443 {"type": "output_text", "text": "foo"}, # sub_index 0
5444 {"type": "output_text", "text": "bar"}, # sub_index 1
5445 ],
5446 }
5447 ```
5448
5449 This is a single item with a shared `output_index` and two sub-indexes, one
5450 for each content block.
5451
5452 This will be processed into an `AIMessage` with two text blocks:
5453
5454 ```python
5455 AIMessage(
5456 [
5457 {"type": "text", "text": "foo", "id": "msg_123"}, # index 0
5458 {"type": "text", "text": "bar", "id": "msg_123"}, # index 1
5459 ]
5460 )
5461 ```
5462
5463 This function just identifies updates in output or sub-indexes and increments
5464 the current index accordingly.
5465 """
5466 nonlocal current_index, current_output_index, current_sub_index
5467 if item_output_indices is not None and item_id in item_output_indices:
5468 output_idx = item_output_indices[item_id]
5469 if sub_idx is None:
5470 if current_output_index != output_idx:
5471 current_index += 1
5472 else:
5473 if (current_output_index != output_idx) or (current_sub_index != sub_idx):
5474 current_index += 1
5475 current_sub_index = sub_idx
5476 current_output_index = output_idx
5477
5478 if output_version is None:
5479 # Sentinel value of None lets us know if output_version is set explicitly.
5480 # Explicitly setting `output_version="responses/v1"` separately enables the
5481 # Responses API.
5482 output_version = "responses/v1"
5483
5484 content = []
5485 tool_call_chunks: list = []
5486 additional_kwargs: dict = {}
5487 response_metadata = metadata or {}
5488 response_metadata["model_provider"] = "openai"
5489 usage_metadata = None
5490 chunk_position: Literal["last"] | None = None
5491 id = None
5492 if chunk.type == "response.output_text.delta":
5493 _advance(chunk.output_index, chunk.content_index)
5494 content.append({"type": "text", "text": chunk.delta, "index": current_index})
5495 elif chunk.type == "response.output_text.annotation.added":
5496 _advance(chunk.output_index, chunk.content_index)
5497 if isinstance(chunk.annotation, dict):
5498 # Appears to be a breaking change in openai==1.82.0
5499 annotation = chunk.annotation
5500 else:
5501 annotation = chunk.annotation.model_dump(exclude_none=True, mode="json")
5502
5503 content.append(
5504 {
5505 "type": "text",
5506 "annotations": [_format_annotation_to_lc(annotation)],
5507 "index": current_index,
5508 }
5509 )
5510 elif chunk.type == "response.output_text.done":
5511 _advance(chunk.output_index, chunk.content_index)
5512 content.append(
5513 {
5514 "type": "text",
5515 "text": "",
5516 "id": chunk.item_id,
5517 "index": current_index,
5518 }
5519 )
5520 elif chunk.type == "response.created":
5521 response = _coerce_chunk_response(chunk.response)
5522 id = response.id
5523 response_metadata["id"] = response.id # Backwards compatibility
5524 elif chunk.type == "response.failed":
5525 response = _coerce_chunk_response(chunk.response)
5526 error_msg = str(response.error or f"Response {response.id} failed.")

5530 raise ValueError(error_msg)

5534 AIMessage,
5535 (

5537 response, schema=schema, output_version=output_version
5538 )
5539 .generations[0]
5540 .message
5541 ),
5542 )

5547 k: v for k, v in msg.response_metadata.items() if k != "id"
5548 }

5552 id = chunk.item.id

5555 content.append(
5556 {
5557 "type": "text",
5558 "text": "",
5559 "phase": phase,
5560 "index": current_index,
5561 }
5562 )
5563 else:
5564 pass

5566 chunk.type == "response.output_item.added"
5567 and chunk.item.type == "function_call"
5568 ):

5570 tool_call_chunks.append(

5572 "type": "tool_call_chunk",
5573 "name": chunk.item.name,
5574 "args": chunk.item.arguments,

5586 }

5600 "computer_call",

5610 ):

5613 tool_output["index"] = current_index
5614 content.append(tool_output)

5617 and chunk.item.type == "custom_tool_call"
5618 ):

     7	    r"""Merge dictionaries.
     8

    10	    dictionaries but has a value of `None` in `'left'`. In such cases, the method uses
    11	    the value from `'right'` for that key in the merged dictionary.
    12	
    13	    Args:
    14	        left: The first dictionary to merge.
    15	        others: The other dictionaries to merge.
    16	
    17	    Returns:
    18	        The merged dictionary.

    20	    Raises:
    21	        TypeError: If the key exists in both dictionaries but has a different type.
    22	        TypeError: If the value has an unsupported type.
    23	
    24	    Example:
    25	        If `left = {"function_call": {"arguments": None}}` and
    26	        `right = {"function_call": {"arguments": "{\n"}}`, then, after merging, for the
    27	        key `'function_call'`, the value from `'right'` is used, resulting in
    28	        `merged = {"function_call": {"arguments": "{\n"}}`.
    29	    """
    30	    merged = left.copy()
    31	    for right in others:
    32	        for right_k, right_v in right.items():
    33	            if right_k not in merged or (
    34	                right_v is not None and merged[right_k] is None
    35	            ):
    36	                merged[right_k] = right_v
    37	            elif right_v is None:
    38	                continue
    39	            elif type(merged[right_k]) is not type(right_v):
    40	                msg = (

    42	                    " but with a different type."
    43	                )

# Responses ingress: client SDK research report

Versions read (sources in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-core/1897327f-fffc-4b34-860d-d276c6197223/scratchpad/sdk-src/`):
- openai-python 3.48.0 (installed). I also downloaded 3.40.0 to `oai340/`. Result: `_streaming.py` and `lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py` are byte-identical in 3.40.0 and 3.48.0. `lib/_parsing/_responses.py` differs by 3 typing-only lines. So the SSE and accumulation models for Python carry over from the 3.40.0 spec. Only the type unions grew.
- openai-node 7.57.0 (`node/package/src/...`).
- langchain-openai 1.8.0 and langchain-core 1.8.0. langchain-openai requires `openai>=2.45.0`, so its SSE decoder is whichever openai-python is installed. I did not diff 2.45.

Nothing was executed. "INFERRED" means I read the code but did not run it.

Paths: `PY` = `.../py/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openai/`. `NODE` = `sdk-src/node/package/src/`.

## 1. openai-python 3.48.0

### SSE decoding (`PY/_streaming.py`)
- **Line ends:** `_SSELineDecoder` splits on CR, LF and CRLF (`_SSE_LINE_END = re.compile(b"[\r\n]")`, L305-335). It carries `_skip_lf` across chunks.
- **BOM:** Each line goes through `raw_line.decode("utf-8")` (L363). I found no BOM handling anywhere. INFERRED: a leading U+FEFF stays in the first line, so the first field name becomes `"﻿event"` or `"﻿data"` and is ignored (L420 "Field is ignored"). Invalid UTF-8 raises `UnicodeDecodeError`.
- **Fields:** `event` and `data` are handled. `data` lines are joined with `\n`. `id` and `retry` are also parsed (L418-437). A comment line starting with `:` is skipped.
- **Dispatch:** An event is emitted only on a blank line (L392-408). `finish()` (L337-341) only decodes the leftover line. It never emits a trailing event. So an event without a final blank line at EOF is DROPPED.
- **Empty events:** An event with only `id:` or `retry:` also dispatches (L393). Its data is `""`, and `json.loads("")` raises `JSONDecodeError`. This also happens for an `event:`-only block.
- **Dispatch key (L70-115):** The code dispatches on `data.type` through the pydantic discriminated union. The `event:` name is ignored, except:
  - When `event` starts with `thread.`, data is wrapped as `{"data","event"}` (L75-92). That would not parse as a Responses event.
  - `event: error` is NOT special in this path. A name that differs from `data.type` is ignored.
- **`[DONE]`:** `sse.data.startswith("[DONE]")` ends the loop quietly (L71). This is a prefix match, so `[DONE]xyz` also ends it. Any later bytes are ignored.
- **`error`:** `is_mapping(data) and data.get("error")` raises `APIError` (L95-107). A Responses `error` event has top-level `code` and `message` and no `error` key. It therefore does NOT raise here. It is passed on as `ResponseErrorEvent`. Only a payload with a truthy `error` key raises.
- **Unknown event types:** `construct_type` (`PY/_models.py:608-674`) falls back to the first union variant. INFERRED: no raise, the object keeps the unknown `.type`. `ResponseStreamState` then passes it through (`_responses.py:397-398`). `ResponseStreamState` has no handling for `error`, `response.failed` or `response.incomplete` beyond passing them through.
- **Bad JSON:** `sse.json()` raises `json.JSONDecodeError` (L94).
- **EOF:** Iteration ends silently. There is no check for a missing `response.completed` at this layer.

### Accumulation (`PY/lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py`, helper `client.responses.stream()` / `ResponseStreamState`)
`responses.create(stream=True)` returns the raw `Stream`. It has no accumulation. LangChain uses this raw path.

The snapshot is keyed by `output_index`. `_output_items: dict[int, item]` (L271, L449) is used for lookup. The snapshot itself is an ordered list.
- **First event (L515-517):** It must be `response.created`, or `RuntimeError`. `_create_initial_response` seeds `_output_items = dict(enumerate(snapshot.output))` (L523).
- **Lifecycle (L407-415):** `created`, `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed` and `incomplete` must carry the same `response.id`, or `RuntimeError("Lifecycle response identity changed.")`.
- **`created`, `queued`, `in_progress` (L417-430):** They may replace `_completed_output` entries that match by identity. A duplicate identity within one event output raises.
- **`output_item.added` (L431-449):**
  - `item is None` is ignored.
  - A repeated `output_index` raises `Duplicate response output index N` (L434-435).
  - Gaps and skips are allowed because the key is a dict. The item is appended as a `function_call` or `message` parsed type, or as-is.
- **`content_part.added`, `output_text.delta`, `function_call_arguments.delta` (L450-465):**
  - They look up by `output_index` only. `item_id` is NEVER checked.
  - A missing index raises `RuntimeError("Received a content event for output index N before receiving its output item")` (`_get_output_item`, L507-513).
  - A wrong item type is silently skipped in accumulation. But `handle_event` then runs `assert output.type == "function_call"` or `"message"` (L305, L345) and raises `AssertionError`.
  - A bad `content_index` gives `IndexError`.
- **`function_call_arguments.done`, `custom_tool_call_input.delta/done`, `output_text.done` (accumulation):** NOT accumulated. They pass through (L397-398). Done events do not replace arguments in the snapshot. Custom tool input is not accumulated at all.
- **`output_item.done` (L466-480):**
  - It records `_completed_output[output_index] = event.item`. The REPLACEMENT is stored separately. The live snapshot is not changed.
  - It raises if the item identity changed against the added item.
  - It raises if the same identity sits at a different index.
  - Identity is `_output_identity` (L242-248). For `function_call`, `custom_tool_call`, `shell_call` and `shell_call_output` it is `(type, None, call_id)`. So `name` and `arguments` may differ between added, done and completed without a raise.
  - An `output_item.done` with no earlier `added` is accepted.
- **`response.completed` (L481-503):** `_completed_response = parse_response(response=event.response)`. The `response.output` from the completed event WINS.
  - Items listed there that were never streamed are accepted.
  - If `output` is `None`, it is rebuilt from `_completed_output` (L495-498). An empty list `[]` is used as-is.
  - For each `_output_items` index with no done item, the final output must contain a compatible item by identity. Otherwise `RuntimeError("Cannot complete response with unfinished output items.")` (L489-494).
  - `parse_response` calls `parse_function_tool_arguments`. With strict tools it does `json.loads(arguments)` (`PY/lib/_parsing/_responses.py:192-217`). That can raise `JSONDecodeError` at completion.
- **`failed` and `incomplete` (L371-396):** Passed through. If `response.output` is None, the event is filled from `_completed_output` or `_output_items`, so partial calls become visible there.

### Raise paths (ResponseStream)
- Non-`created` first event.
- Lifecycle id change.
- Duplicate `output_index`.
- Content event before `added`.
- `AssertionError` for a wrong item type.
- `IndexError` for a bad `content_index`.
- Done identity change.
- Conflicting identity position.
- Unfinished items at `completed`.
- `JSONDecodeError` at `parse_function_tool_arguments`.
- `APIError` from a payload with an `error` key.
- `JSONDecodeError` or `UnicodeDecodeError` at the SSE layer.
- `get_final_response()` raises `RuntimeError("Didn't receive a response.completed event.")` (L86-95) after `failed`, `incomplete` or truncation.

### Final tool calls
`get_final_response()` returns `_completed_response`, which is built from `response.completed.response.output`. It is NOT the live snapshot. The live snapshot only feeds the `snapshot=` fields of delta events and the synthetic `failed` or `incomplete` outputs. A client that reads `output_item.done`'s `event.item` sees `item.call_id`, `name`, `arguments` and `id` as sent in that event. Function call fields: `arguments`, `call_id`, `name`, `id` (optional), `namespace`, `async`, `caller` (`types/responses/response_function_tool_call.py:35-59`). Custom tool call fields: `call_id`, `input`, `name` (`response_custom_tool_call.py:31-40`).

## 2. openai-node 7.57.0

### SSE decoding (`NODE/core/streaming.ts`, `NODE/internal/decoders/line.ts`)
- **Line ends:** CR, LF and CRLF. Event chunks split on a double newline (`findDoubleNewlineIndex`, L193+). `\r` is also stripped at L683.
- **BOM:** `decodeUTF8` uses `TextDecoder` (`internal/utils/bytes.ts:29-37`). INFERRED: by WHATWG default, each per-line decode strips a leading BOM. Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD and does not raise. This differs from Python.
- **Dispatch:** `SSEDecoder.decode` (L682-725) handles only `event` and `data`. `id` and `retry` are ignored. It emits when `event` or `data` is non-empty. `flush()` (L593-596, L733) emits a pending trailing event at EOF, which Python does not.
- **`[DONE]`:** `sse.data === '[DONE]'` is an exact match (L137). It breaks the loop.
- **`JSON.parse`:** A failure throws `SyntaxError('Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.')` (L144-149).
- **Legacy mode (default; `streamMode` set in `internal/parse.ts:32-47`):**
  - `event.startsWith('thread.')` yields `{event, data}` (L152-156). This has no `type`, so the accumulator throws.
  - `sse.event === 'error'` throws `APIError` (L158-160).
  - A payload with a truthy `data.error` throws `APIError` (L162-164).
  - So an `event:` name of `error` raises even if `data.type` says otherwise.
- **Dispatch key:** `data.type`. The `event:` name is used only as above.

### Accumulation (`NODE/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` plus `NODE/internal/responses/response-accumulator.ts`)
- **`error` event type (`ResponseStream.ts:476-483`):** `if (event.type === 'error') throw new APIError(...)`. This is a raise for a Responses `error` event, even though Python passes it through.
- **Unsupported types (`response-accumulator.ts:567-587`, `supportedResponseEventTypes` L472-540):** A type outside the set throws `OpenAIError('Unhandled response stream event: unknown')`. The set contains the listed output events plus `keepalive`, `error`, `response.audio.*`, `response.compaction.compacting`, `response.mcp_list_tools.*`, `response.image_generation_call.partial_image`.
- **First event:** Must be `response.created` (L1377-1384).
- **Keying:** Wire `output_index`, mapped to snapshot position (`ResponseStream.ts:262-292`, via `#outputPositions`).
  - `added` with a repeated or completed index throws `Duplicate response output index N`.
  - A negative or non-integer index throws.
  - Gaps are allowed. The `added` item is appended at the next position (L278).
  - A non-`added` event with an unknown index throws `missing output at index N`.
- **`item_id` is validated** (`response-accumulator.ts:386-434`). For every item-scoped event, `item_id` must be non-empty and equal the output item's `id`, or `expected item_id ... got ...` is thrown. A wrong item type is also rejected. A `function_call` without `id` therefore cannot take item-scoped delta events.
- **Item identity checks (`getOutputItemIdentityKeys`, L202-234):**
  - `id` must be a non-empty string, except for `function_call` and `custom_tool_call` where it is optional.
  - `function_call` needs a `call_id`.
  - A duplicate `id:` or `call:<type>:<call_id>` identity throws (L236-241).
- **`done` events REPLACE:**
  - `function_call_arguments.done` sets `output.arguments = event.arguments` (L938-943).
  - `custom_tool_call_input.done` sets `output.input = event.input` (L952-958).
  - `output_item.done` calls `replaceResponseOutputItem` (L627-654), which validates type, id and `call_id` first and then overwrites the whole item at that position.
  - Deltas append to `arguments` and `input` (L931-937, L945-951). `mcp_call_arguments.*` is handled the same way.
- **`response.completed`:**
  - `#prepareEvent` (`ResponseStream.ts:210-258`) fills a missing `output` from `#completedOutput` (done items only).
  - It then runs `#assertComplete` (L302-324). Every added-but-not-done item must have a replacement in `completed.output` with matching identity, or `Cannot complete response with unfinished output items.` is thrown.
  - Then `cloneValidatedResponse` replaces the WHOLE snapshot with the completed response (`response-accumulator.ts:1389-1391`), after the identity validators.
  - So `completed.output` wins. Calls never streamed are accepted.
  - An empty `output: []` is accepted if every added item was done.
- **`created`, `queued`, `in_progress` (L500-519, `#updateInterimResponse`):** They merge into the snapshot by identity.
- **`failed` and `incomplete`:** Not special-cased beyond filling `output` from all items, partial ones included (L237-241).
- **Raise sites:** `error` event, unsupported type, bad or duplicate index, `item_id` mismatch, identity mismatch on `done` or `completed`, unfinished items, a lifecycle `response.id` change, a missing `response` field on a lifecycle event, and `content_index` or content type errors. All are thrown from `#addEvent`. Every one of them happens BEFORE `maybeEmit('event', ...)` (L542) of that event. Earlier events were already emitted.

- **Line ends:** CR, LF and CRLF. Event chunks split on a double newline (`findDoubleNewlineIndex`, L193+). `\r` is also stripped at L683.
- **BOM:** `decodeUTF8` uses `TextDecoder` (`internal/utils/bytes.ts:29-37`). INFERRED: by WHATWG default, each per-line decode strips a leading BOM. Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD and does not raise. This differs from Python.
- **Dispatch:** `SSEDecoder.decode` (L682-725) handles only `event` and `data`. `id` and `retry` are ignored. It emits when `event` or `data` is non-empty. `flush()` (L593-596, L733) emits a pending trailing event at EOF, which Python does not.
- **`[DONE]`:** `sse.data === '[DONE]'` is an exact match (L137). It breaks the loop.
- **`JSON.parse`:** A failure throws `SyntaxError('Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.')` (L144-149).
- **Legacy mode (default; `streamMode` set in `internal/parse.ts:32-47`):**
  - `event.startsWith('thread.')` yields `{event, data}` (L152-156). This has no `type`, so the accumulator throws.
  - `sse.event === 'error'` throws `APIError` (L158-160).
  - A payload with a truthy `data.error` throws `APIError` (L162-164).
  - So an `event:` name of `error` raises even if `data.type` says otherwise.
- **Dispatch key:** `data.type`. The `event:` name is used only as above.

### Accumulation (`NODE/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` plus `NODE/internal/responses/response-accumulator.ts`)
- **`error` event type (`ResponseStream.ts:476-483`):** `if (event.type === 'error') throw new APIError(...)`. This is a raise for a Responses `error` event, even though Python passes it through.
- **Unsupported types (`response-accumulator.ts:567-587`, `supportedResponseEventTypes` L472-540):** A type outside the set throws `OpenAIError('Unhandled response stream event: unknown')`. The set contains the listed output events plus `keepalive`, `error`, `response.audio.*`, `response.compaction.compacting`, `response.mcp_list_tools.*`, `response.image_generation_call.partial_image`.
- **First event:** Must be `response.created` (L1377-1384).
- **Keying:** Wire `output_index`, mapped to snapshot position (`ResponseStream.ts:262-292`, via `#outputPositions`).
  - `added` with a repeated or completed index throws `Duplicate response output index N`.
  - A negative or non-integer index throws.
  - Gaps are allowed. The `added` item is appended at the next position (L278).
  - A non-`added` event with an unknown index throws `missing output at index N`.
- **`item_id` is validated** (`response-accumulator.ts:386-434`). For every item-scoped event, `item_id` must be non-empty and equal the output item's `id`, or `expected item_id ... got ...` is thrown. A wrong item type is also rejected. A `function_call` without `id` therefore cannot take item-scoped delta events.
- **Item identity checks (`getOutputItemIdentityKeys`, L202-234):**
  - `id` must be a non-empty string, except for `function_call` and `custom_tool_call` where it is optional.
  - `function_call` needs a `call_id`.
  - A duplicate `id:` or `call:<type>:<call_id>` identity throws (L236-241).
- **`done` events REPLACE:**
  - `function_call_arguments.done` sets `output.arguments = event.arguments` (L938-943).
  - `custom_tool_call_input.done` sets `output.input = event.input` (L952-958).
  - `output_item.done` calls `replaceResponseOutputItem` (L627-654), which validates type, id and `call_id` first and then overwrites the whole item at that position.
  - Deltas append to `arguments` and `input` (L931-937, L945-951). `mcp_call_arguments.*` is handled the same way.
- **`response.completed`:**
  - `#prepareEvent` (`ResponseStream.ts:210-258`) fills a missing `output` from `#completedOutput` (done items only).
  - It then runs `#assertComplete` (L302-324). Every added-but-not-done item must have a replacement in `completed.output` with matching identity, or `Cannot complete response with unfinished output items.` is thrown.
  - Then `cloneValidatedResponse` replaces the WHOLE snapshot with the completed response (`response-accumulator.ts:1389-1391`), after the identity validators.
  - So `completed.output` wins. Calls never streamed are accepted.
  - An empty `output: []` is accepted if every added item was done.
- **`created`, `queued`, `in_progress` (L500-519, `#updateInterimResponse`):** They merge into the snapshot by identity.
- **`failed` and `incomplete`:** Not special-cased beyond filling `output` from all items, partial ones included (L237-241).
- **Raise sites:** `error` event, unsupported type, bad or duplicate index, `item_id` mismatch, identity mismatch on `done` or `completed`, unfinished items, a lifecycle `response.id` change, a missing `response` field on a lifecycle event, and `content_index` or content type errors. All are thrown from `#addEvent`. Every one of them happens BEFORE `maybeEmit('event', ...)` (L542) of that event. Earlier events were already emitted.

### Final tool calls
`finalResponse()` (L700-707) returns `#endRequest`, which is the live snapshot (replaced by `completed.response` if it arrived). A clean EOF after at least one event resolves without `completed` and returns the PARTIAL snapshot. That snapshot can include a function call with partial arguments. The docstring says so: "A clean end after at least one response event resolves even when the response is incomplete" (L694-699). If the stream is cut by an exception, `finalResponse()` rejects. `maybeParseResponse` (`ResponsesParser.ts:189+`) adds `parsed_arguments`. It may parse arguments for auto-parseable tools. INFERRED: that parse can throw on invalid JSON.

## 3. LangChain (langchain-openai 1.8.0 / langchain-core 1.8.0)

### Path
`ChatOpenAI._use_responses_api` returns true when `use_responses_api` is true, or when the payload has built-in tools or any of `context_management, include, previous_response_id, reasoning, text, truncation` (`base.py:4629-4641`). Streaming calls `self.root_client.responses.create(**payload)` with `stream=True` (L1711-1735). That is the raw openai-python `Stream`, so section 1's SSE rules apply. There is no SDK accumulation. LangChain accumulates through `AIMessageChunk.__add__`.

### Chunk conversion (`_convert_responses_chunk_to_generation_chunk`, `base.py:5408-5721`)
- **Dispatch key:** `chunk.type`.
- **Routing:**
  - `item_id` is taken from `chunk.item.id` or `chunk.item_id` (L5422). The first `output_index` seen for each `item_id` is pinned (`setdefault`, L5430).
  - `_advance` (L5432-5476) uses the pinned index when the `item_id` is known. It increments `current_index` when the output index changes.
  - So routing is by `item_id` first, then `output_index`. There is NO validation that the item type is a function call.
- **Function call chunks:**
  - `output_item.added` with `item.type == "function_call"` makes a `tool_call_chunk` with `name`, `args=item.arguments`, `id=call_id` and `index=current_index` (L5565-5595).
  - `function_call_arguments.delta` makes a chunk with `args=delta`, no name and no id, at `current_index` (L5632-5639).
  - `function_call_arguments.done` and `output_item.done` (function_call) fall into the `else` and are IGNORED (L5698-5699). Done events never replace arguments.
- **Custom tool calls:** Only `output_item.done` with `custom_tool_call` is used. It makes a chunk with `args=json.dumps({"__arg1": item.input})` (L5615-5631). The `custom_tool_call_input.*` events and the `added` event are ignored.
- **Built-in items on `output_item.done`:** `web_search_call`, `file_search_call`, `computer_call`, `code_interpreter_call`, `mcp_call`, `mcp_list_tools`, `mcp_approval_request`, `image_generation_call`, `tool_search_call`, `tool_search_output`, `apply_patch_call`, `apply_patch_call_output`, `compaction` become content blocks only (L5596-5614). They are NOT tool calls.
- **`local_shell_call` and `shell_call`:** Appear in neither list. They are dropped in both streamed and non-streamed paths.
- **Raises (`ValueError`):**
  - `response.failed` raises `ValueError(str(response.error or "Response <id> failed."))` (L5524-5527).
  - `error` raises `ValueError("<code>: <message>")` (L5528-5530).
  - On `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`, `_construct_lc_result_from_responses_api` raises `ValueError(response.error)` when `response.error` is set (L5202-5203).
  - Also raise: `AttributeError` if `chunk.item` is None on `added`/`done`, and any openai-python SDK raise from section 1 (`APIError`, JSON or UTF-8 errors).
  - `response.incomplete` is NOT a failure. It is handled like `completed`.
  - `created`, `queued`, `in_progress` and unknown event types are ignored (`created` only sets the id).
- **Completed event:** Only `usage_metadata`, `parsed`, `response_metadata` and `chunk_position="last"` are taken (L5531-5549). The built message content and `tool_calls` are NOT emitted. `completed.response.output` therefore does NOT affect streamed tool calls. Streamed tool calls come only from `added` plus deltas, plus `done` for custom calls.

### Merge and conversion (langchain-core)
- **Merge (`langchain_core/utils/_merge.py:98-177`, `merge_lists`):** Items with an integer `index` merge when the index matches AND the ids are not inconsistent (`id` is None or `""` on either side, or equal; L130-137). Merged by `merge_dicts` (L6-95):
  - String fields are CONCATENATED (L64). That covers `name` and `args`. Only `id` and `output_version` are exempt if equal.
  - Same-index chunks with differing non-empty ids stay separate entries.
  - A repeated `added` for the same output index with the same `call_id` would concatenate `name` (`"fnfn"`) and `args`. INFERRED from this code.
  - A delta for an `item_id` never seen on `added` registers a new index. It becomes its own chunk with `name=None` and `id=None`.
- **`tool_calls` (`messages/ai.py:509-572`, `init_tool_calls`):** This model validator runs on every `AIMessageChunk` construction, so also on every partial sum. Each `tool_call_chunk` goes through `parse_partial_json` (`utils/json.py:60+`). It closes open strings and braces. The result is:
  - A dict becomes a `tool_calls` entry with `name or ""`. So a PARTIAL call appears in `tool_calls` at any prefix.
  - A non-dict value or an exception goes to `invalid_tool_calls` (`error=None`).
  - An empty `args` string becomes `{}`.
  - This is the main reason the "no partial call at a client raise" rule matters for LangChain. At a `ValueError` mid-stream, the caller's last accumulated chunk already exposes a partial call.
- **Non-stream path (`_construct_lc_result_from_responses_api`, L5195-5382):**
  - Uses `response.output`. `function_call` goes to `tool_calls` if `json.loads(arguments, strict=False)` succeeds. Otherwise it goes to `invalid_tool_calls` with `error=str(e)` (L5285-5307).
  - `custom_tool_call` goes to `tool_calls` with `args={"__arg1": input}` (L5308-5316).
  - `response.error` truthy raises `ValueError`.
  - `local_shell_call` and `shell_call` are dropped.
  - Usage comes from `response.usage` (L5237-5242).

## 7. Cross-SDK comparison

| Aspect | openai-python 3.48 (stream helper) | openai-node 7.57 | LangChain 1.8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dispatch key | `data.type`; `event:` ignored (except `thread.`) | `data.type`; `event: error` raises; `thread.` breaks | `chunk.type` (python SDK raw stream) |
| BOM | not stripped (INFERRED); U+FEFF kept, field ignored | per-line `TextDecoder` strips (INFERRED) | as python |
| Invalid UTF-8 | raises | U+FFFD, no raise | as python |
| EOF event without blank line | dropped | flushed (L593) | as python (dropped) |
| `[DONE]` | `startswith`, stop | exact match, stop | as python |
| `error` event | passed through, no raise (no `error` key) | raises `APIError` | raises `ValueError` |
| `response.failed` | passed through; final raises | accumulated; final resolves or rejects | raises `ValueError` |
| `response.incomplete` | passed through | accumulated | like `completed` |
| Unknown event type | passed through | raises (except 6 ignored) | ignored |
| Keying | `output_index` (dict) | wire `output_index` to position; `item_id` validated | `item_id` first (pinned), then `output_index` |
| Item type check on delta | `assert` after accumulate | strict raise | none |
| `output_index` repeated | raises | raises | merged by index+id |
| Skipped index | allowed | allowed | allowed |
| `.done` event | recorded in `_completed_output` only; live snapshot unchanged | REPLACES arguments, input and item | ignored for function_call; used for custom |
| `custom_tool_call_input.*` | not accumulated | accumulated, `.done` replaces | ignored |
| `completed.output` | final response built from it; wins | replaces whole snapshot; wins | ignored for tool calls |
| Final call source | `get_final_response()` (completed) | live snapshot, replaced at completed; partial if truncated | `added` + deltas (+ custom `done`) |
| Raise conditions | see section 1 | see section 2 | see section 3 |
| Partial call exposure at a raise | `ResponseOutputItemDoneEvent` item already yielded; no partial in final | snapshot internal; events emitted before the raise | `parse_partial_json` puts partial args in `tool_calls` |

## 8. Implications for invariant I1 (INFERRED from the code above)
1. The final source differs per SDK. Python uses `completed.output`, Node uses the snapshot replaced by `completed`, and LangChain uses `added` + deltas. The gateway must make `added`, deltas, `done` and `completed.output` agree. This covers `name`, `call_id` and `arguments`, and also the item `id`.
2. In Python, identity is `(type, call_id)`. A `completed.output` call with a new `call_id` is accepted without a raise. The gateway must decide Allow for every call that is in `completed.output` and in every `output_item.done`.
3. `added.arguments` is non-empty in LangChain: `args=item.arguments` is concatenated with all deltas. A non-empty `added.arguments` plus deltas gives a different string than Python or Node would accumulate. Keep `added.arguments=""` or keep all views consistent.
4. LangChain routes by `item_id`, Node validates `item_id == output item id`, Python ignores `item_id`. A delta whose `item_id` differs from the item at its `output_index` is a divergence trap. Emit consistent ids.
5. A partial call is visible in LangChain at every prefix, in the Node snapshot, and in Python's `failed` or `incomplete` event output. If the gateway raises or truncates mid-call, all three expose partial calls unless the call is withheld until decided.
6. Client-executed items beyond `function_call` (`custom_tool_call`, `computer_call`, `local_shell_call`, `shell_call`, `apply_patch_call`, `tool_search_call` with `client`, `mcp_approval_request`) need the same decide-before-emit treatment. LangChain hides some of them from its tool-call surface, but the other SDKs expose them.
7. The `error` event is a raise in Node and LangChain and a passthrough in Python. A gateway abort with a Responses `error` event gives different client states per SDK.
